No fixed sleeps in tests (oculist-l6m.32).

title: Dispersion Bloom beacon effect: palette-derived radial chromatic dispersion
description: Add a new beacon effect to effectsRegistry (content.js:577) reproducing the look known in shader terms as radial chromatic dispersion / prismatic refraction / iridescent ripple. Design was brainstormed and specified 2026-08-26; only the final build approval was outstanding. DESIGN DECISION ALREADY MADE BY THE HUMAN: hues are DERIVED FROM THE ACTIVE PALETTE, not a true spectrum. A real R-G-B rainbow split conveys via hue, which is exactly what tritanopia/deuteranopia/protanopia users cannot separate, and Oculist's vision profiles exist to prevent that. So the effect splits around getEffectiveColors().beacon rather than the full spectrum: it stays colourblind-safe and consistent with the profiles, and reads as an iridescent dispersion bloom rather than a prism. Do not re-litigate this. SHAPE, mapping the three shader steps to DOM plus the Web Animations API: (1) UV distortion becomes an expanding ripple - three concentric rings centred on the match rect, scaling outward across getBeaconDuration(). (2) Channel offsetting becomes hue-offset rings - take getEffectiveColors().beacon, run it through hexToHsl, emit three rings at hue -22, 0, +22 degrees, the same idiom animateFlame already uses at content.js:1103-1106. Each ring gets a slightly different end scale and a small stagger, and that separation IS the dispersion. (3) Radial attenuation becomes progressive blur and fade - each ring animates filter: blur() outward while opacity falls, softening the separation toward the edge. (4) Additive recombination - the rings sit in a container with isolation: isolate and blend plus-lighter against each other ONLY, so they recombine bright at the core and split into iridescent bands at the fringe without blending into the host page, which would make the effect vanish on white backgrounds. Confirm plus-lighter against the manifest's Chrome floor (needs 111+) and fall back to screen if needed. NO WEBGL: this is a content script on arbitrary pages, every existing effect is DOM plus WAAPI, and a canvas adds compositing and CSP surface for something that fires once per active match. The isolate plus plus-lighter pairing reproduces the additive recombination a shader would do. WIRING is one function, one i18n label, one registry line - the in-page settings panel auto-enumerates effectsRegistry at content.js:3848, so no popup HTML change. INHERITED FREE, no code needed: animate() already returns early when motion is off and routes to animateReducedMotion when reduced, so this never fires under reduced motion; cancelBeacons() already sweeps .oc-beacon; and it enters no vision preset, so it is never auto-enabled. LITE MODE: three rings drop to one, matching warpDrive's ringCount = settings.performanceMode ? 1 : 3. DONE: the effect is selectable in the settings panel and renders a palette-derived dispersion bloom on the active match; a test asserts the ring hues track getEffectiveColors().beacon rather than a hardcoded spectrum when the profile changes; a test asserts all beacon elements are removed by the end (no leak); a test asserts reduced motion yields the reduced-motion beacon and never the rings; a test asserts Lite Mode drops the ring count. Use condition polling, not waitForTimeout - oculist-l6m.32 converted 156 fixed sleeps and a new one regresses it. Photosensitivity note: a single expanding pulse per activation, no repeat or flash, keeps this clear of WCAG 2.3.1's three-flash threshold; do not add looping or strobing.

title: Poll timeout budget of 5000ms is insufficient on contended hardware
description: Found during oculist-l6m.32 review. After the sleep-to-poll conversion (commit e97e029), parallel suite runs on a contended machine fail with isolated waitForFunction timeouts rather than wrong-value assertions: post-change 2/7/2 failures across three runs, versus pre-change 0/2/3. The failing test differed every run, and one failing file (chip_count_accessibility.test.js) is not touched by that diff at all, which points at the poll budget rather than at any specific conversion. test/helpers/wait.js defaults to a 5000ms timeout with a 30ms interval, and page.waitForFunction calls use Playwright's own default. The implementer deliberately declined to blanket-raise 5000ms to 10000ms on the grounds that a wide timeout increase masks real regressions, which is correct - a slow test that still passes tells you nothing. The right fix is probably not a global bump: consider a single configurable budget read from an env var so CI and contended dev boxes can raise it without changing what the suite asserts, leaving the default tight enough that a genuine regression still surfaces as a timeout quickly. MEASURE FIRST on an idle machine (this box was at load average 39-46 on 10 cores from unrelated work when the above numbers were taken) - the problem may not exist at all under normal conditions. Blocked-by relationship: resolving oculist-l6m.32's open load clause likely resolves or obviates this. Also fold in a small fix while here: test/chip_row.test.js:184's addTerm() helper gained an acceptance branch on 'any .oc-notice exists' which is load-bearing (4 cap/notice tests fail without it) but unscoped to the cap notice, so any test where a stray notice lingers gets a no-op wait. Scope the selector to the cap notice.

title: Malformed saved lists are invisible in the panel but still occupy one of the 50 list slots
description: Found during oculist-l6m.35 review. listSavedLists (content.js:263) excludes any entry failing its Array.isArray(entry.terms) shape guard, and readListIndex counts every oc-list-* key toward MAX_SAVED_LISTS regardless. So a corrupted entry (terms: 'nope', terms: null, a bare 'not-an-object' value, or a numeric id) is invisible in the saved-lists panel yet still consumes one of the 50 slots, with no way for the user to see or delete it. l6m.35 deliberately kept this conservative: its done-criteria were about the three gates agreeing on what 'empty' means, which is a different question from shape validation, and relaxing only the Array.isArray guard would fix roughly a quarter of the problem while leaving the other malformed shapes just as invisible. Needs a coherent policy decided as a whole: render anything carrying a usable id and name as a disabled row so rename/delete stay reachable, and/or stop counting unrenderable junk toward the cap. NOTE for whoever takes this: the pinned test 'listSavedLists() skips junk under the prefix instead of throwing' in test/list_storage.test.js documents old behaviour rather than encoding a deliberate contract - its real intent is 'does not throw', and its length === 1 assertion is a mechanical side effect of the shape check. Amend it rather than treating it as a blocker. Done: a malformed-but-identifiable saved list is either visible and deletable, or does not consume a slot; a test covers each malformed shape.

title: No change listeners on prefers-color-scheme, prefers-contrast or prefers-reduced-motion, so OS setting flips leave injected CSS stale
description: Found during oculist-l6m.28 review. All three media queries in content.js are poll-on-read with no change listener: getActiveThemeName() (content.js:545) reads matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches fresh per call, and prefersMoreContrastQuery (content.js:4691, from oculist-l6m.17) and reducedMotionQuery (content.js:2122) follow the same pattern. Confirmed by grep: no addEventListener('change') on any media query anywhere in content.js. Consequence: the per-call read is genuinely live, but nothing re-invokes injectHighlightStyles() when the OS setting flips, so a user switching their OS to dark mode (or enabling increased contrast, or reduced motion) mid-session keeps the previously injected CSS until some unrelated event happens to trigger a re-inject. l6m.28 fixed the resolution bug and its test proves the live read works when the function IS called; this bead covers making it get called. Fix: attach change listeners to the three media queries and re-run injectHighlightStyles() on fire. Note oculist-l6m.17's contrast gate has the same exposure, so this affects the dim treatment too. Done: flipping the OS colour scheme, contrast preference, or reduced-motion preference mid-session updates the injected CSS without any other user action; a test emulates each flip and asserts the CSS changes.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: CLOSED via commit da4e589. Two of the three named flips got change listeners; the third is a proven no-op, not an omission. IMPLEMENTED: prefersMoreContrastQuery and reducedMotionQuery were already module-level singletons; prefers-color-scheme was not (getActiveThemeName called window.matchMedia fresh per invocation, so there was nothing to attach to), so a module-level colorSchemeQuery singleton was introduced and getActiveThemeName now reads colorSchemeQuery.matches. One addEventListener('change') per singleton re-runs injectHighlightStyles(). REDUCED-MOTION IS A NO-OP BY CONSTRUCTION, verified empirically rather than by reading: a probe snapshotted both injected stylesheets, flipped reducedMotion to reduce, and re-snapshotted with nothing else done. #oc-global-highlight-styles was byte-identical and contains no token matching /motion|prefers-reduced/i at all; #oc-dialog-styles was byte-identical with 'oc-no-motion' appearing exactly twice before and after (one static rule at content.js:5464-5468, emitted unconditionally). A listener would be a literal no-op re-inject and a CSS-diff test would have nothing to diff. The done-criteria's literal 'the CSS changes' wording is UNSATISFIABLE for this flip, not unimplemented. The bead's INTENT is satisfied: behaviour does update live, probed at 23 beacon parts on full motion, 0 after the flip, 23 restored, because effectiveMotion() (content.js:2180-2184) reads reducedMotionQuery.matches fresh per render, so there is no staleness window. That is already covered by test/prefers_reduced_motion.test.js:93. VERIFIED: retained MediaQueryList.matches confirmed live in-page; registration cannot stack (module scope, behind the top-of-file re-injection guard at content.js:4) and cannot fire before boot() (a change event cannot interrupt the synchronous IIFE); post-destroy flips throw nothing and leave exactly 1 global style element, and that element is present on every page at HEAD anyway; 15 alternating flips produced no style stacking. Suite 118 pass / 0 fail, no new waitForTimeout so oculist-l6m.32 is not regressed. KNOWN RESIDUE, deliberate: the listeners are not removed in __ocDestroy() (content.js:663), matching the existing chrome.storage.onChanged pattern, so a torn-down instance keeps re-injecting an inert style element on every OS flip for the page's lifetime.

title: Flaky: lite_mode_restore.test.js draft-ownership assertion fails intermittently under full-suite load
description: Found during oculist-l6m.42 review. One uncontrolled full-suite run hit AssertionError: 'the draft must own oculist-match while it is non-empty' at test/lite_mode_restore.test.js:225. Not seen in 10 subsequent controlled runs (5 on the working tree, 5 at detached HEAD), so it is rarer than oculist-nw4's resize flake. Recorded so the suite's flakiness is known to extend beyond the resize test rather than being written off as a single bad test. Same family as oculist-nw4 and oculist-l6m.32: readiness and wall-clock dependence under parallel load. Needs a repeat-run harness to characterise before fixing.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: LEFT OPEN deliberately after the oculist-l6m.32 conversion (commit e97e029). The implementer reported this bead as 'addressed as part of the general lite_mode_restore.test.js conversion', with no repro attempted since it was already rare. The reviewer judged that honest but not evidence: nothing in that diff targets this flake specifically and no test demonstrates it is gone. Closing would be closing on faith. The general conversion did replace lite_mode_restore.test.js's fixed waits with debounce-result polling, so this may well be fixed - it just is not shown. NEXT STEP: run the suite repeatedly on an idle machine (this flake was seen once in ~16 full runs, so it needs a repeat-run harness to characterise) and close only if it does not reappear. Related: oculist-nw4 and oculist-mmm were both closed by that same commit with verified root-cause fixes.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: CLOSED on differential evidence, no code change required - this bead was resolved by oculist-l6m.32's sleep-to-poll conversion (commit e97e029). MECHANISM: the assertion moved to test/lite_mode_restore.test.js:358. Before the conversion, typeDraft() was fill() plus a fixed waitForTimeout(400) against a 400ms debounce plus a rescan, i.e. zero margin, then the test read CSS.highlights.get('oculist-match') once and asserted. That is exactly the described flake. Now the assertion is preceded by waitForContentScriptValue polling the SAME expression with the SAME predicate the assertion checks, at 30ms intervals with a 5000ms budget, so the value asserted on is by construction one that satisfies the predicate. The named AssertionError is structurally unreachable; the only reachable failure is a poll timeout, which raises a different, self-describing error. POSITIVE CONTROL, which is what actually closes this: the reviewer restored the pre-conversion file as a temp probe and ran both versions under 12 CPU burners at load average ~45. OLD version, 8 runs: 1 FAIL with the bead's exact symptom, reproduced verbatim on demand. CURRENT version, 14 runs under identical load: 14/14 pass. The load condition demonstrably reproduces the flake on old code and not on new, which is a differential rather than an absence of evidence. Corroboration: 62 total runs of the current code across orchestrator and reviewer, zero reproductions. NOTED STRICTNESS LOSS, not a blocker: the old test asserted ownership was correct at T+400ms; the new one asserts it becomes correct within 5s. A regression that merely DELAYS draft ownership by up to 5s would now pass. That is correct semantics for a debounced pipeline, but the invariant is enforced by the poll's timeout rather than by the assert line, which is a tautology of the poll.

title: Two fixed 300ms sleeps in active_match_magnifier.test.js are unprincipled and under-sized
description: Found during oculist-l6m.42 review. The two tests added for l6m.42 use page.waitForTimeout(300) at test/active_match_magnifier.test.js:566 and :620 to settle a race before toggling settings. The implementer added them to fix a reported false-negative negative control, but the reviewer could not reproduce that false negative: reducing the settle wait to 0ms still produced a clean negative-control failure 3/3. Worse, the scroll path defers up to 600ms (content.js:3269), so 300ms does not even cover the branch these tests take. The waits are 'usually-green' rather than principled. Fix: replace both with a condition-based wait on the actual readiness signal. The underlying production race (a deferred animate() at content.js:3293 reading settings at fire time, so a late animate can draw the card on its own) is benign and not worth its own bead - a setting applying a few ms early is not user-visible. Fold into oculist-l6m.32 if that bead is taken first.

title: Flaky: 'repositions on resize' test in active_match_magnifier.test.js intermittently fails under full-suite load
description: During full 'npm test' runs (not isolated), test/active_match_magnifier.test.js's 'repositions on resize instead of stranding in old document coordinates' test intermittently fails with 'card should start centered on the match, dx=-476...ms' — a large offset suggesting the 100ms resize debounce/reflow hadn't settled within the 5000ms waitForFunction window under full-suite CPU contention. Reproduced on 2 of 4 full-suite runs (2026-08-26); passes reliably in isolation (node --test test/active_match_magnifier.test.js). Unrelated to oculist-l6m.42's fix — observed both before and after that change. Likely needs a more generous timeout or a more robust readiness check than the current dx<6 poll.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: CORRECTION - the diagnosis in this bead's description is wrong and will send an implementer to the wrong line. Established during the oculist-l6m.42 review with 10 controlled full-suite runs (5 on the working tree, 5 on a detached HEAD worktree; the resize test failed 0/5 in BOTH, so the flake did not reproduce under controlled conditions at all). The failing assertion is assert.ok(Math.abs(before.dx) < 6, ...) at test/active_match_magnifier.test.js:415, which runs BEFORE any resize happens - so the cause is not an unsettled 100ms resize debounce. The real cause: the readiness gate searchUntilMagnifierWord() polls only the card's TEXT and never its POSITION, so the test proceeds while the card is still at stale coordinates. Fix direction: make the readiness gate assert on position as well as text. Also NOT the same root cause as oculist-l6m.32 - this test uses waitForFunction throughout rather than fixed sleeps, so l6m.32's '106 fixed sleeps' framing does not cover it, though both are the same family of readiness/wall-clock dependence.

title: loadWorkList mount restore writes workListTerms/activeTermIndex without a rescan, so the .20 invariant does not literally hold
description: Found during oculist-l6m.15 review. content.js:4550 (the loadWorkList mount-restore callback) is a 0-to-N workListTerms transition that does NOT call performListSearch() and does NOT reset termRanges - it calls renderChipRow() directly. It is safe today only by virtue of __ocDestroy (content.js:674) zeroing termRanges, and every reopen routing through it, so termRanges is provably [] at that point. Only a theoretical race could beat it (a chrome.storage.session callback losing to a 150ms input debounce plus a 350ms mutation debounce), which in-memory storage makes unreachable in practice. The issue is that the invariant comment landed by oculist-l6m.20 at content.js:2521 states 'every writer of activeTermIndex must call performListSearch() synchronously after setting it', and this call site does not do that. Either route this site through the rescan, or amend the comment to name the __ocDestroy-zeroing exception explicitly. Leaving it as-is means the documented invariant is subtly false, which is the exact failure mode .20 was closed to avoid.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: STOPPED after two failed reviews, left IN_PROGRESS with work UNCOMMITTED on branch epic/oculist-followups. The production change PASSED both reviews and is correct; the test file is what failed, twice, in the same way. PRODUCTION (good, verified twice, content.js SHA-256 020be66f...dccb06 byte-identical across both reviews): content.js:4670 sets termRanges = [] explicitly in the loadWorkList mount-restore callback, making the site locally correct rather than dependent on __ocDestroy zeroing it. The oculist-l6m.20 invariant comment at content.js:2620-2628 was amended to allow two legal forms, and the reviewer verified it is now literally true of all 9 activeTermIndex write sites: :646 init and :742 __ocDestroy and :4194 loadSavedList and :4666 mount-restore all satisfy form 2 (set termRanges consistently), while :3080 activateChip and :3098/:3100/:3102 removeChipAt and :3187 addChipTerm satisfy form 1 (synchronous performListSearch). No writer satisfies neither. REVIEW 1 FAILURE: the no-scan assertion was decorative - injecting a real buildPageIndex() into the restore path left the suite green, because the getComputedStyle baseline was captured after the restore had already completed. Fixed in the second pass via installRestoreProbe(), which brackets the callback synchronously inside a patched chrome.storage.session.get; the reviewer reproduced that injecting buildPageIndex() now correctly fails with 3 !== 2. That part is genuinely fixed. REVIEW 2 FAILURE, still outstanding: the out-of-range test's NAME and comment claim it pins normalizeWorkList's clamp, and the describe header repeats the claim. It does not. The reviewer deleted the clamp at content.js:108 and the suite stayed 5/5 green, proving the mutation was live with a peek hook showing activeTermIndex = 99 at the callback. The test stays green only because of renderChipRow's tolerance (isActive = i === activeTermIndex never matching), which the comment explicitly disclaims as not being what it tests. Both halves of the comment are backwards, and the previous vaguer name was net better than the new specific-but-wrong one. TO FINISH: either assert the observed index is -1 (a value-level assertion that diverges at 99), or strip the mechanism claim from the test name, its comment, and describe-header claim (3), describing it as what it is - an end-to-end no-throw/no-active-chip render check that does not distinguish sanitizer from renderer. Nit: the comment cites normalizeWorkList at content.js:102-109; it is actually at 103-110. NOTE THE PATTERN worth human attention: on a bead whose entire subject is documentation promising what the code does not enforce, the implementer shipped exactly that defect twice.

title: Toggling a vision setting does not redraw the current match
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.39 review. Pre-existing, shared by magnifier and textLabels.

The chrome.storage.onChanged listener (content.js:5355-5360) does not call
repositionActiveOverlays(), so flipping Match Labels or the new Magnifier toggle does not swap
the overlay in or out on the match currently on screen. The change only appears on the next
navigation or redraw.

A user toggling the setting to see what it does gets no feedback and reasonably concludes it is
broken.

Done: a vision-settings change redraws the active match's overlays in place; a test toggles the
magnifier with a match on screen and asserts the card appears without navigating.

title: Nothing tests the magnifier's font scaling or truncation
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.39 review. The code is correct (the reviewer verified it at
content.js:1975-1979) but no test protects it.

Untested:
- font-size derived from the MATCH's own computed font-size x 2.5, clamped to 16-48px. This was
  called out in the bead as the point most likely to be got wrong, precisely because bead .11
  records the same mistake being made with getBeaconScale() for chip sizing. A regression here
  would be silent.
- the ~24-character truncation with ellipsis for long matches.

Also minor, same file: test/active_match_magnifier.test.js shares one browser page across the
whole file, so one failure cascades into later tests. Harmless while green, noisier when red.

Done: tests pin the x2.5 derivation, both clamp bounds, and the truncation; the suite isolates
its page per test or resets state between them.

title: Chip accessible-name tests assert the raw attribute and skip two states
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.16 review. The behaviour is correct (the reviewer verified it live via
the CDP accessibility tree), but the committed tests are weaker than the verification was.

1. test/chip_count_accessibility.test.js:145 and :156 assert getAttribute('aria-label'), the raw
   attribute, rather than the computed accessible name. Those differ whenever name computation
   changes precedence, which is exactly the kind of regression this test exists to catch.
2. No test covers the two subtle states: a cap-starved chip (skipped because the total match cap
   was hit, lands in the sparse-array undefined bucket and must announce no count) and a Lite Mode
   chip (announces the real count from countMatchesOnly). Both were verified by hand only, so a
   regression in either would go unnoticed.

Done: the assertions read the computed accessible name, and both the cap-starved and Lite Mode
states have coverage.

title: restoreActiveChip claims 'no match' for an unscanned chip via the input debounce
description:
Found during the oculist-l6m.19 re-review. Same false-claim class as the regression .19 fixed,
reached through a different entry point, so .19's guard does not cover it.

restoreActiveChip (content.js:2499-2501) writes i18n.noMatch for an unscanned chip when
reached via the INPUT DEBOUNCE rather than via findNext. Repro: against a restored but
unscanned working list, type a draft then clear the input. The debounce fires,
restoreActiveChip runs, and the count reads "no match" for a chip whose term may well have
matches on the page, because it has never been scanned.

Count and nav still agree (nav disabled, nothing highlighted), so this is cosmetic, but it is
the extension stating something false about the page.

The distinction .19 established is the fix: termRanges[i] === undefined means never scanned
(show blank), an empty array means scanned with genuinely zero matches (show "no match").
Apply the same test here.

Done: an unscanned chip restored via the debounce path shows a blank count, not "no match";
a test covers type-then-clear against a restored unscanned list.

title: welcome.js localStorage fallback contradicts the privacy policy
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.10 review. Low severity, pre-existing.

extension/welcome.js:665,672 read and write localStorage['oc-settings'], which contradicts
PRIVACY.md's statement that Oculist writes to no storage area other than the ones listed.

It is a dead fallback branch: chrome.storage.sync is always defined on an extension page, so
no user data actually lands in localStorage. But the policy sentence is absolute and the code
is not.

Done: delete the dead branch, or soften the policy sentence to match. Deleting is preferable,
since an absolute privacy claim is worth more than an unreachable fallback.

title: loadSavedList does not clear the pending search debounce
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.9 review.

loadSavedList (content.js:3615) does not clearTimeout(debounceTimer). Typing a draft and then
loading a list inside the 150ms debounce window lets the debounce fire afterwards with
input.value === '', reaching restoreActiveChip() -> performSearch('') with
activeTermIndex === -1.

Benign today (it clears to the empty state) but it is an unintended scan-adjacent call on a
path whose whole contract is "loading runs no scan".

Done: loadSavedList clears the pending debounce; a test loads a list mid-debounce.

title: Theme hover colour reads settings.theme instead of the resolved theme
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.9 review. Three sites, same mistake, fix together.

content.js:4888 (new, from .9), :4303 and :4741 (both pre-existing) use
settings.theme === 'dark' rather than the already-in-scope resolved activeTheme (:4176).
Under theme 'system' with a dark OS, the hover tint renders the light-mode value.

Done: all three use the resolved theme; a test covers system-theme + dark OS.

title: Saved-list storage rough edges
description:
Three minor findings from the oculist-l6m.8 review.

1. deleteList (content.js:378) reuses the SAVE failure message on a delete failure, so a
   failed delete tells the user "delete a saved list and try again". Needs its own string.
2. readListIndex (content.js:272-277) counts junk keys toward the 50-list cap, while
   listSavedLists hides them. A corrupted oc-list-* key could block saving while the user
   sees fewer than 50 lists and cannot work out why.
3. Note only, not fixable with the chrome.storage API: an inherent TOCTOU between the cap
   read (content.js:304) and the write (content.js:314) means two devices sitting at 49
   lists can both pass the check.

Done: 1 and 2 fixed, 3 recorded as a comment where the race lives.

title: Saved-list storage: three untested branches
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.8 review. The behaviour is correct (the reviewer verified all three
by hand via a CDP probe) but the suite does not cover them, so a regression would ship silently.

1. generateListId's collision loop (content.js:217-226) has ZERO coverage. The existing
   assertion notStrictEqual(second.list.id, first.list.id) passes even if the function
   ignored existingIds entirely.
2. The 10-term and 100-char caps in sanitizeListTerms are untested, despite being a stated
   done-criterion of .8. Verified by hand: 16 terms in -> 10 out, 150-char term -> exactly 100.
3. The 50-list cap test catches a permissive off-by-one (> vs >=) but not an over-strict one,
   because no test saves the 50th list successfully.

Done: each of the three has a test that fails against the corresponding wrong implementation.

title: Consolidate the six window.__oc* test-only hooks
description:
Do this AFTER oculist-l6m.9, so the UI tests exist and can make some hooks redundant.

There are now six test-reachability hooks on the isolated-world window: __ocLoadWorkList and
__ocSaveWorkList from .2, plus __ocSaveList, __ocListSavedLists, __ocRenameList, and
__ocDeleteList from .8. Plus the pre-existing __ocToggle and __ocDestroy, which are a real
call path and stay.

Two reviews have now confirmed empirically that these land in the extension's isolated world
and are undefined in the host page, so this is not a security issue. It is accumulating
production surface that exists only for tests, and .2's review already warned against growing it.

The hooks were genuinely necessary: they are IIFE closures, CDP Runtime.evaluate only reaches
globals, and testing through chrome.storage directly would test Chrome's API rather than this
code.

Done: the six test-only hooks are collapsed into a single window.__ocTest namespace, or
deleted where .9's UI tests reach the same behaviour through the interface.

title: Match-cap feedback is misleading in two ways
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.7 review. Both are user-facing copy/affordance problems, not logic
errors.

1. The notice reads "Showing the first 2000 matches. Remove a term for a complete count."
   but the cap is checked BEFORE materialising each term, so the real total can reach 2997.
   The new cap test documents this. The number in the message is simply not true. This
   string came from the v1.7.0 design doc, so the spec is the source of the error.
   Fix direction: say "Showing about the first 2000 matches" or check the cap after
   materialising and report the real figure.

2. A starved chip (skipped because the cap was hit) renders a BLANK count, which is visually
   identical to "not scanned yet" (content.js:2591). The cap notice mitigates this globally
   but the two per-chip states are indistinguishable, so the user cannot tell which terms
   were actually skipped.
   Fix direction: render a distinct marker on starved chips.

Done: the notice states a number that matches reality, and a starved chip is visually
distinct from an unscanned one.

title: traverse() duplicates a narrower check instead of using isOculistNode()
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.4 review.

The self-match fix added an identity check `child !== wrap` to traverse(). It is sufficient
today, because traverse() starts at document.body and every beacon, marker, and label is
mounted on document.documentElement, while oc-global-highlight-styles is a <style> already
covered by SKIP_TAGS.

But it is a partial duplicate of the existing isOculistNode() helper and will silently miss
any future Oculist-owned node mounted under body. The next person to add one gets phantom
matches with no failing test.

Done: traverse() routes through isOculistNode(), or the identity check carries a comment
explaining why it deliberately does not.

title: Chip sizing keys off getBeaconScale(), the beacon knob
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.3 review.

Chip text size is derived from getBeaconScale() (the vision-profile beacon size s/m/l/xl).
At xl (2.25) chip text renders at 27px. That is the only scale hook in content.js, but it
is the BEACON knob, not a UI-text knob, so chip sizing is riding on an unrelated setting.

Needs a design decision: either introduce a separate UI-text scale, or clamp the chip
scale, or accept the coupling deliberately and comment it.

Done: chips render at a sensible size across all four beacon sizes, and whichever way it
is resolved is recorded in a comment.

title: Release chores for v1.7.0
description:
Steps:
1. Bump repo/extension/manifest.json version to 1.7.0.
2. Add a 1.7.0 entry to repo/CHANGELOG.md describing multi-term lists, saved lists, and the
   carry-over behaviour.
3. Confirm no new manifest permissions were added. 'storage' was already granted, so there
   is no new Chrome Web Store permission justification to write. If a permission did creep
   in, stop and report rather than shipping it.
4. Run `npm test` and `npm run build`, and confirm the zip builds.

Done: version bumped, changelog entry present, permissions unchanged, tests and build pass.
notes:
BLOCKING ADDITION from the .9 review — PRIVACY.md is now factually wrong and this is a Chrome Web Store disclosure issue, not a docs nit.

PRIVACY.md currently states, all three of which are false as of v1.7.0:
- 'Everything Oculist stores lives in chrome.storage.sync under a single key, oc-settings'
  -> saved lists now live under their own oc-list-<id> keys
- 'writes to no other storage area'
  -> the working term list lives in chrome.storage.session
- 'keeps no history of what you searched for'
  -> saved lists ARE a persisted, cross-device-synced record of search terms

Update PRIVACY.md to describe all three storage areas accurately and to state plainly that
saved lists persist search terms and sync across the user's devices. Check docs/privacy.html
for the same claims and keep the two consistent.

NOTE: PRIVACY.md, docs/index.html and docs/privacy.html have uncommitted edits that predate
this epic and are unrelated to it. Do not sweep them into your commit. Report what you find
there rather than reverting or committing someone else's in-progress work.

title: Fix clipped box-shadow glow on Impact Burst effect
description: In repo/extension/content.js, animateImpactBurst()'s burst-shape element has both clip-path (for the star polygon) and box-shadow (for glow) — clip-path clips box-shadow, so the glow never renders. Move the glow to a separate unclipped element behind the star, or drop the box-shadow. Cosmetic only, found during review of oculist-y9h.1.
close_reason: Obsolete — the Impact Burst effect (oculist-y9h.1) was reverted in 2554612, so animateImpactBurst() and its clipped box-shadow no longer exist in extension/content.js. Re-file if the effect is ever reintroduced.

title: Lens: the 1200px source height cap is covered by no test
description: Inverse of oculist-wwu, found by the same reviewer with the opposite mutation. wwu made animateLens's body/html bail independently provable via a short-body fixture. Running the mutation the other way - deleting BOTH height caps (extension/content.js:1666 and the in-walk 'candRect.height <= 1200' at :1641) while leaving the bail intact - leaves the FULL suite green at 145/145. So the cap is now the unproven guard: nothing anywhere fails if it is removed or broken. FIX: add a fixture where the match's nearest non-inline ancestor is a real element (NOT body) taller than 1200px, so the bail cannot fire and the cap is the only guard in play. Assert the lens falls back to the match's immediate parent rather than cloning the oversized ancestor. DONE: deleting the 1200px cap alone fails a test. RELATED NOTE from the same review: the wwu test's 'lens did not mount' branch passes vacuously if the lens fails to draw for an unrelated reason (finder not focused, Enter swallowed). Not vacuous today - mutation proves it bites - and a contention flake would surface as a false failure rather than a false pass, so this is a robustness note, not a correctness bug.

title: Bloom: nothing asserts ring end scales or DOM order
description: Found during the oculist-4qt review by mutation probe. Reversing BOTH ringHueOffsets and ringEndScales in animateDispersion's full-mode path (so -22 pairs with end scale 24.5 instead of 18) leaves the entire suite GREEN, 4/4. Two blind spots cause it: (1) test/dispersion_bloom.test.js:373 sorts the offsets before comparing, so ring DOM order is invisible to the assertion; (2) assertColorsMatch is documented as order-independent; and (3) nothing anywhere in test/ asserts the end-scale values 18/21/24.5 at all. So the 'three rings at -22/0/+22 with end scales 18/21/24.5, in that order' contract is verified only by reading the code. The Lite Mode case is the exception - its offset-0/scale-21 pairing is structurally guaranteed by the shared centred slice, so it needs no separate pinning. FIX: assert the end scales (readable from each ring's animation keyframes or a data attribute if one is added), and compare offsets in DOM order rather than sorted. DONE: reversing the offset/scale arrays, or mispairing an offset with the wrong end scale, fails a test. SEPARATE MINOR ITEM from the same review: for ringCount > 3 the centred-slice arithmetic yields a negative ringStart, so slice(-1, 3) silently under-renders (ringCount 4 or 5 draws ONE ring, not four). No undefined or NaN, so it is safe, but quietly wrong. Clamp with Math.max(0, ringStart) or add a comment naming the ceiling, if ringCount ever becomes tunable.

title: Lens: the body/html bail and the 1200px source cap mask each other in tests
description: In animateLens (extension/content.js ~1600), two guards stop the effect cloning the whole document: an unconditional bail when the resolved sourceEl is document.body/documentElement, and a ~1200px height cap on the resolved source. In test/lens_effect.test.js the fixture body is ~2000px tall, so removing the bail alone still leaves the suite green (the height cap catches it instead); only removing BOTH turns it red. The assertion is not vacuous, but the bail is not independently mutation-provable. FIX: add a fixture page with a SHORT body (under 1200px) carrying a bare text-node match directly under <body>, so the bail is the only guard in play and removing it goes red on its own. Found by the reviewer on oculist-y6a, ruled non-blocking. DONE: removing the body/html bail alone fails a test.

title: Dispersion Bloom's Lite Mode ring uses the -22 hue offset, not the base palette hue
description: In animateDispersion (extension/content.js:1381-1383), the ring loop indexes hueOffsets by r. With ringCount = 1 under Lite Mode (settings.performanceMode), the single rendered ring therefore takes hueOffsets[0] === -22 rather than the base 0 offset — so Lite Mode users see the beacon shifted 22 degrees off getEffectiveColors().beacon instead of the palette colour itself. Still palette-derived and still colourblind-safe, so this is cosmetic, not an accessibility defect. FIX: when ringCount === 1, emit the 0 offset (e.g. pick the middle of the offsets array, or slice the offsets to a centred subset sized to ringCount). Also add a length guard so endScales/hueOffsets indexing cannot silently yield undefined/NaN colours if ringCount ever grows past the array length — safe today only because it is always 1 or 3. Found by the reviewer on oculist-dvv, ruled non-blocking. DONE: Lite Mode renders one ring at the unshifted palette beacon hue, and a test pins it.

title: renameList silently discards a malformed terms value with no user notice
description: Found during oculist-dzi review. renameList (content.js:386) does terms: Array.isArray(existing.terms) ? existing.terms : [], so renaming an entry whose terms is malformed silently replaces it with an empty array. The user gets no notice that data was discarded. This path was unreachable before oculist-dzi, because malformed entries were invisible in the panel and so had no reachable rename button; dzi made them visible and deletable, which also made this the one user-reachable lossy path it opened up. dzi corrected the comment at content.js:363-366 so the behaviour is at least documented, which was the actual ask there, but the silence to the user remains. Normalising garbage on an explicit user write is defensible and matches the 0-terms badge the panel already shows, so this is low priority. Options: leave as-is now that it is documented; surface a notice via showNotice with its own key (the per-class notice machinery from oculist-l6m.12 makes this cheap); or preserve the unknown value so a user could recover it. Done: renaming an entry with malformed terms either tells the user the value was discarded, or preserves it.

title: traverse()'s text-node branch still duplicates isOculistNode() with an ad-hoc oc-beacon check
description: Found during oculist-l6m.14 review. content.js:2248 (the text-node branch of traverse()) still uses an ad-hoc parent.classList.contains('oc-beacon') instead of routing through isOculistNode(), which is the last remaining duplicate of that helper inside traverse() after l6m.14 fixed the element branch. It is currently dead defense rather than a live gap: any Oculist ancestor is now rejected before descent, so the text-node branch can no longer be reached for Oculist-owned text. Worth collapsing for the same reason l6m.14 existed - the duplicate will silently diverge from isOculistNode() if the helper gains a new marker. Done: the text-node branch routes through isOculistNode(), or carries a comment saying why it deliberately does not.

title: X-button chip removal briefly shows the removed term's count and highlights for one debounce tick
description: Found during oculist-l6m.33 review, verified with a live probe. Removing the only chip via the X button while a search debounce is still in flight (<150ms) shows the removed term's stale count and highlights for one debounce tick, then self-heals to the draft's correct state. Transient, self-limiting, and internally consistent throughout - the count, nav state and highlights agree with each other at every instant, they are just briefly the removed term's. Not a done-criteria failure for .33; filed as polish. Fix would be to cancel or invalidate the in-flight debounce on X-button removal the way the Backspace path already resets lastTerm (content.js removeChipAt, ~line 3003).

title: Whitespace-only stored terms render an enabled load control that does nothing
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.26 review. Corrupted or hand-edited storage only, non-destructive.

Three gates disagree about what counts as an empty term list:
- buildListItem (content.js:3753) gates on raw list.terms.length
- loadSavedList (content.js:3682) gates on sanitizeListTerms(...).length
- listSavedLists (content.js:250) filters to strings without trimming

So a stored list with terms: ['   '] renders an ENABLED load control badged "1 term", and
clicking it is a silent no-op, because loadSavedList sanitizes the whitespace away and hits
its empty early-return.

Not reachable by saving through the UI, since saveList now rejects empty-after-sanitize.
Reachable via hand-edited or corrupted sync storage.

Done: the three gates agree on one definition of empty, applied consistently.

title: Dead assertion and missing dedupe defence from .6
description:
Two one-liners found during oculist-l6m.6 review.

1. test/dim_highlight.test.js:204 asserts priorities.dim === 0, but 0 is the CSS spec default
   for Highlight.priority, so deleting the assignment at content.js:1977 can never fail it.
   The assertion cannot detect what it appears to test.
2. normalizeWorkList (content.js:102-109) does not dedupe terms. updateDimHighlight skips the
   active term BY INDEX, not by text, so a session payload with a repeated term would put the
   active term's own ranges into the dim set. Unreachable through the UI today because
   addChipTerm dedupes on add.

Done: the assertion tests something real or is removed with a comment saying why; normalizeWorkList dedupes.
notes:
THIRD ONE-LINER from the .5 review: the else branch inside the committed-Enter block (content.js:2833-2836) is unreachable, because performListSearch() always sets firstEnter = true when searchRanges.length > 0. Remove it or explain why it stays.
FOURTH ONE-LINER from the .7 review: the Lite Mode toggle rescan (content.js:4232) fires even when the bar is closed and wrap is null, paying a full buildPageIndex() for no visible effect. Guard on wrap.
FIFTH ONE-LINER, from the .19 re-review: content.js:2680-2689 nests if (!hasActiveChip) inside if (!term) where if (!term && !hasActiveChip) reads better. Cosmetic only.
SIXTH ONE-LINER, from the .27 review: .oc-settings-reset-btn's accessible name is the literal string '↺ Reset', so the glyph leaks into what a screen reader announces. Move the glyph out of the accessible name.
